text: The game is really fun, but the time spent preparing ingredients is even longer than the time needed to complete a level, and the preparation process is very repetitive. Please consider adding some machines with automatic cutting or stove upgrades, as well as rack upgrades, to improve the gaming experience. Right now, we’re just playing to clear levels rather than truly enjoying the gameplay.

I love playing this game with my friends but it KILLS ME to see AI generated slop all over, especially as a graphic artist. Hopefully with the money they receive from buyers of this game, they'll actually pay artists to update their typography and rat icons shown throughout the game.

When I look at Steam reviews of this game, I see a lot of people calling out the usage of AI and the developers deny all claims. But if you simply take a screenshot of the AI generated image/type and put it through an AI image detector, it always comes back as a 90%+ rating as "yes" it was AI generated. Again, I love playing this game with my friends but it kills me to support AI slop.

Almost a good game. It's very confusing because all the ingredients for a fun game are there, but the way they present them is honestly terrible. At first it's pretty fun but once things settle and you understand it as a game, it feels like the developers screwed something up along the way, or just didn't playtest the game much before shipping.

My main issue: you spend 3ish day cycles where nothing changes at all. Once you finally get a chance to upgrade the restaurant, you are presented with a choice that is completely random. The problem is, you could get 3 very boring or terrible choices, and furthermore, it just doesn't feel like enough changes. You can unlock a new dish, but then the player doing the waiting has to spend another 3 days doing nothing new. If you buy new furniture for the customers, the player in the kitchen has no perception of anything changing. So really you have to sometimes wait 6 whole days before even a minor change happens in gameplay, often more, if, say, you get 2 dishes in a row or something like that. And sometimes the upgrade you get is the ability to buy pre-cut veggies or something.

Other things
- I am like 36 days into career mode and we have yet to unlock a dish that brings vampires or ghosts. So we have less gameplay variety just because the randomized card rewards are that bad.

As it stands; I wouldn't recommend it. I thought the gameplay was neat, but kept checked the storepage at some point. No AI disclosure. After a bit of playtime, checked out some comments to confirm there's AI usage. Was going to continue playing with a friend, because another friend posted a thread on reddit where the developer (Alyssa) confirmed AI use, BUT that it would be replaced by real artists. Figured ok, when they go through with that, I'll buy the game.

Went through some more steam reviews, to find the same developer seeming to claim 'There's no AI in the game', as well as links to spotify and the trailer, and the credits. Everything was done by artists (this was November). 
In game's discussions, there's been an update in their discord as of July 2025, stating there IS AI in the game, but it's meant as a placeholder due to being a small team.
I don't really get if that just means they added the AI later, or something was miscommunicated in November or what happened, but it really killed my mood for the game entirely to have to run around for something that should be a disclaimer on the main store page. 

I don't know if there's a reason the AI wasn't admitted to in November, nor if there's a particular reason it isn't labelled on the base page. May revisit this once the placeholders are gone, but I really dislike how unclear it seems to be. Im not a fan of Generative AI, and I know a lot of people don't care, but at the very least I expect it to be said when it's u

my friend and i played this game for several hours last night and had a lot of fun! i enjoy games like this a lot and the gameplay scratches an itch in my brain.

but i was thoroughly disappointed by the egregious use of AI-generated imagery, and even more disappointed to find out that there is no disclosure of its usage anywhere and the devs' shady behavior surrounding it (eg. denying usage of AI even though it's extremely obvious). for this reason, i cannot in good faith recommend this game until this is addressed by the devs properly, even though i had fun with it.

additionally, i didn't know about the MAGA accessory in-game nor the dismissive attitude the developers took when it was brought up until i checked out other reviews. this left a bitter taste in my mouth as both an american and has someone who has been negatively impacted by this political movement.

all in all, i'd call it wasted potential.

Genuinely thought this game must've been in early access because of the lack of content and wonky, not fully fleshed out mechanics. The skill tree is just repeated full of the same uncreative perks and doesn't fully lean into its potential, making it feel boring and stale after just a few hours of playing. The cooking mechanics are complex enough to be fun, but the setup requires at least one person hosting and one person cooking - the hosting player will consistently receive less XP comparatively and have just enough to do to not justify running the long trek to the kitchen. Something that would help with this is allowing the drink jugs to be placed in the dining rooms too, as a "bartender" kinda vibe, so the host player could at least fulfill drink requests this way. Additionally, not sure how to see reputation, or how that impacts the restaurant, but we've had to buy multiple of the "call extra customer" furniture items because otherwise we'd just be standing around waiting for more customers despite empty seats and positive reviews. The rate at which you earn the ability to buy new items is also a bit frustratingly slow, and are random, so it often feels like a way to make the game feel longer with less content. Also I do not believe "roguelike/"roguelite" is an accurate descriptor, so just fyi if that is important to you. Their content roadmap has no dates, w

Where to begin with this?
First off, whatever happened to Steam's AI content policy? You know, where developers have to disclose when their games contain AI content? Because there is a lot of it in this game, and it was not mentioned anywhere on the store page.
Second, this game is so badly optimized and buggy as to be borderline unplayable. My friends and I couldn't even finish the tutorial because it bugged and wouldn't let us serve the second guest. Not to mention the laggy controls, making everything feel super slow and clunky, the random lag spikes that are entirely too common for such a small game even with my PC specs, and the completely unintuitive gameplay.
My friends and I were hoping for a silly, fun experience. What we got was broken AI slop.
Just get Ale & Tale Tavern. At least that one is actually fun.

If you're not affected by the MAGA movement, and don't care about the cosmetic, it's a fun game for friends. If you don't support MAGA or are bothered by it being included in the game, I don't recommend buying it.

Fundamentally, I think the game is relatively fun and hectic, the same sort of fun you would get from those supermarket simulator style games.

I believe the progression could be improved, it feels just a bit slow during the prep time and a bit too fast during serving hours. How are 3 rats supposed to handle two couriers and a VIP hitting nearly all at the same time? Completely insurmountable task for I believe was day 17 or so.

The reason my review is negative is simple, I simply do not agree with AI generated assets being used in games, and I definitely don't like that there was no disclaimer for it on the store page. I've read the comments prior to writing this review, and I'm not the only one who's noticing; I've also noticed the dev says "there is no AI in our game" which is unfortunate because the dev either does not know it's AI and was lied to about it by an artist, or is outright lying themselves. The most prominent gen AI asset I've seen is the skill tree rat in the center. I believe the title text "RESTAURATS" was AI assisted, but those are the only two notable AI generated assets I've spotted.

In my opinion, it's better to outright replace art that people are calling AI generated even if it's not AI generated, because it will keep getting negative reactions from people who are against it.

(or at the very least, replace it with better looking AI assets!)

Me and my friends were excited to try this game out for the free weekend event. We love finding those good old friendslop games with prox chat and plenty of chaos to throw around. Like PEAK and Super Battle Golf. Well, we were sadly mistaken about this one.

Not only does the game feel ENTIRELY unoptimized, it overrides my mic settings in-game so all my friends and I top out our mics and it's unpleasant to say the least. Not to mention the very obvious ai "art" slop found throughout the game that's ENTIRELY undisclosed to us.

We didn't even get to finish the tutorial before the game broke entirely, making it unplayable. We lost interest very quickly after that.

It's not worth your time. I'm glad I didn't buy this game.

Not recommended right now, as future updates and changes would easily make this game top tier 
 
Cons: 
- Prep time far exceeds actual game play. 30 mins of prep with only 10 min of game play is not an optimal ratio 
- Lacks difficulty, slow progression rate causing it to seem repetitive  
- Too much down time in between rounds and sometimes during the round itself. 
- Expenditure often exceeds income, capping your progression further - e.g. ingredients often costs at least half the income you received during the previous round. In addition accumulating tax in this game (even on owning furniture) further caps your income - (tax seems way too high in this game; if you are going to have such realistic tax brackets, should introduce a way to mitigate tax, which would be an interesting aspect to consider as it is not seen in other cooking games) 
 
Pro: 
- Game looks great, cool concept and character designs, great mechanics 
- Nice range of customisation  
- Runs smooth with rare glitches

Gameplay is just too slow, upgrades seem impossible to gather, had 4 of us bored after 2 hours since the fourth guy had literally nothing to do except wash dishes which is not alot, for its price I would much rather push people to other games in this genre personally.

Edit: seen the reply about devs stating AI art was removed (still looks sussy but ill take their word on it)

As for the AI allegations, dev seems to have proven that at least the trailer wasn't AI made, so I didn't look further, but after playing, in-game menu assets really do feel very GenAI, the Rat face on the back of the Cards and the Rat on the skill tree look very close to outputs you could get from public GenAI models, the way the dev speaks about how this is placeholder art makes it feels like they may not be completely honest about the game's lack of AI Disclosure.

I would have never gotten this game if I had known there was AI in it. I unfortunately got it because they didn't add that section to their description, which I'm pretty sure goes against Steam's TOS. You could have gotten artists to help with making the logo and trailers, labels for the boxes, and other places that I may not have seen the AI slop generated at, but they chose not to. I am completely and utterly disgusted and disappointed.

Regardless, from the bit I played before realizing this, it was pretty hectic, a lot needs to be improved about it (i.e.: not enough space in the kitchen, recipes take too long to make, the UI is all over the place and does not make sense, the goblin takes way too long to deliver things and they only deliver it one at a time, etc..). It's a fun game for sure, but gets tiring. Played for 4 hours, only made it to day 14 and level 8. The trailer shows a lot of quirkiness and events, but we've only had 2 random events, both lasting less than 2 minutes, and there is no quirkiness outside of the theme. Progression is slow, the margins you make from dishes is realistic (not extremely fun in a fantasy game), there's taxes on furniture? Why? I only make ~200-800 a day and I'm taxed 100 just from a few shelves and tables.  
 
Also, the graphics are decent, but are terribly optimized. I have a 3070 and i7-11800H. I can run BF6 at 90+ fps on medium, but I can't run this at 70+ on high. Constant dips into the 30fps range. Somehow this culminates into piercing headaches.  
 
Overall, it's a fantasy cooking game that doesn't take itself serious, but takes the mechanics of cooking and finances very serious. Slow progression and not a lot of rewards make it tiring. Probably should be closer to $10-15 given the amount of content.
